import pandas as pd

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_3.csv"
source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_4.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)
df4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History:
# 1) JOIN : [["Source5_44_4", "Source5_44_1"], ["Cust_id", "Cust_id"]]
df_join_1 = pd.merge(df4, df1[['Cust_id', 'Customer_Segment']], how='left', left_on='Cust_id', right_on='Cust_id')

# 2) JOIN : [["Source5_44_4", "Source5_44_0"], ["Ord_id", "Ord_id"]]
df_join_2 = pd.merge(df_join_1, df0[['Ord_id']], how='left', left_on='Ord_id', right_on='Ord_id')

# 3) JOIN : [["Source5_44_4", "Source5_44_2"], ["Prod_id", "Prod_id"]]
df_join_3 = pd.merge(df_join_2, df2[['Prod_id']], how='left', left_on='Prod_id', right_on='Prod_id')

# 4) JOIN : [["Source5_44_0", "Source5_44_3"], ["Ord_id", "Ship_id"]]
# Note: This join is between Source0 and Source3 on Ord_id = Ship_id
# We need to join df0 and df3 first, then join the result back to df_join_3 on Ord_id and Ship_id

# Join Source0 and Source3 on Ord_id == Ship_id
df0_3_join = pd.merge(df0, df3, how='left', left_on='Ord_id', right_on='Ship_id')

# Now join df_join_3 with df0_3_join on Ord_id and Ship_id
# df_join_3 has columns Ord_id and Ship_id
# df0_3_join has Ord_id and Ship_id (Ship_id from df3)
# We join on df_join_3.Ord_id == df0_3_join.Ord_id and df_join_3.Ship_id == df0_3_join.Ship_id

df_final = pd.merge(df_join_3, df0_3_join[['Ord_id', 'Ship_id']], how='left',
                    left_on=['Ord_id', 'Ship_id'], right_on=['Ord_id', 'Ship_id'])

# After all joins, select and rename columns to match target schema:
# Target Schema: ['Customer_Segment': string, 'Ord_id': integer, 'Prod_id': integer, 'Ship_id': integer, 'Cust_id': integer]
# The source columns are string IDs like 'Ord_1', 'Prod_1', 'SHP_1', 'Cust_1', so we need to convert them to integers by extracting the numeric part.

def extract_int_id(s, prefix):
    if pd.isna(s):
        return pd.NA
    if isinstance(s, str) and s.startswith(prefix):
        return int(s[len(prefix):])
    return pd.NA

# Extract integer IDs from string IDs
df_final['Ord_id'] = df_final['Ord_id'].apply(lambda x: extract_int_id(x, 'Ord_'))
df_final['Prod_id'] = df_final['Prod_id'].apply(lambda x: extract_int_id(x, 'Prod_'))
df_final['Ship_id'] = df_final['Ship_id'].apply(lambda x: extract_int_id(x, 'SHP_'))
df_final['Cust_id'] = df_final['Cust_id'].apply(lambda x: extract_int_id(x, 'Cust_'))

# Select columns in target schema order
target_df = df_final[['Customer_Segment', 'Ord_id', 'Prod_id', 'Ship_id', 'Cust_id']]

# Drop rows with any missing values in these key columns to ensure data integrity
target_df = target_df.dropna(subset=['Customer_Segment', 'Ord_id', 'Prod_id', 'Ship_id', 'Cust_id'])

# Convert data types to match target schema
target_df['Customer_Segment'] = target_df['Customer_Segment'].astype(str)
target_df['Ord_id'] = target_df['Ord_id'].astype(int)
target_df['Prod_id'] = target_df['Prod_id'].astype(int)
target_df['Ship_id'] = target_df['Ship_id'].astype(int)
target_df['Cust_id'] = target_df['Cust_id'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/target_multisource.csv"
target_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source5_44_4 with Source5_44_1 on Cust_id
df = pd.merge(source4, source1, on="Cust_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source5_44_0 on Ord_id
df = pd.merge(df, source0, on="Ord_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source5_44_2 on Prod_id
df = pd.merge(df, source2, on="Prod_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source5_44_3 on Ship_id
df = pd.merge(df, source3, on="Ship_id", how="inner")

# Group by Customer_Segment to ensure uniqueness as per FD and target key
df = df.groupby("Customer_Segment", as_index=False).first()

# Select only the target columns in the correct order and types
# Target schema: ['Customer_Segment': string, 'Ord_id': integer, 'Prod_id': integer, 'Ship_id': integer, 'Cust_id': integer]
# Convert Ord_id, Prod_id, Ship_id, Cust_id to integer by extracting numeric part after underscore

def to_int_id(col):
    return df[col].str.extract(r'_(\d+)$').astype(int)

df["Ord_id"] = to_int_id("Ord_id")
df["Prod_id"] = to_int_id("Prod_id")
df["Ship_id"] = to_int_id("Ship_id")
df["Cust_id"] = to_int_id("Cust_id")

# Keep Customer_Segment as string
result = df[["Customer_Segment", "Ord_id", "Prod_id", "Ship_id", "Cust_id"]]

# Write to CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
